mainTopic: How strong a גזירה שוה is depending on its free words, and the reasons behind רבי מאיר's view on animal-shaped miscarriages
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about גזירה שוה: a comparison whose words are מופנה (extra) on both sides beats one that is מופנה on only one side. רב אחא בריה דרבא then gives a more lenient version of רבי אלעזר's rule, and the גמרא explains what difference it makes for רבנן. It also shows the logical refutation that knocks down the comparison between a person and a sea monster. Next the גמרא looks for the reason behind רבי מאיר's view that a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus is טמאה לידה. It offers several reasons: the word יצירה, eyes like a person's, and eyes that face forward. Each reason is challenged and defended. אביי says רבי מאיר's bird case means only owls, and the גמרא works through two ברייתות about birds. Finally, רבי ירמיה asks a joking question about betrothing such a creature, and the גמרא returns to רב's statement that רבי מאיר counted it only because its kind can live. רב ירמיה מדפתי's comment on that statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the animal comparison is free on both sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. We learn from the comparison that is מופנה on both sides, and the תורה made the animal comparison that way on purpose, so we would not learn from the weaker one-sided comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learn from the comparison that is free on both sides. That is why the Merciful One made the animal comparison free on both sides: so that we would not learn from the comparison that is free on only one side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer that began just before this. Two comparisons were competing, and we follow the one that is מופנה on both sides: the comparison to an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison is מופנה when its key words are extra and not needed in their own place, so they are free to teach something new. The more free words a comparison has, the stronger it is. The תורה deliberately made the animal comparison free on both sides so that it would beat the sea-creature comparison, which is free on only one side.

keyTerms.meaning: Free: the word in the פסוק is extra and not needed in its own place, so it is available to teach a comparison
On both sides: the extra word is free in both פסוקים being compared
On one side: the word is free in only one of the two פסוקים
The Merciful One: a way of referring to ה׳ as the One who gave the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how 'free' the words are is a way to decide between two comparisons that point in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And we derive from the analogy that is free on both sides.
And for this reason the Merciful One made it free
the analogy of animal, on both sides,
so that we would not derive
from the analogy that is free on one side.
phrases.notes: The comparison to a sea creature, the weaker one discussed just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous section about which comparison we follow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking of sources: the stronger comparison overrides the weaker one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have learned from the sea-creature comparison, which is מופנה on one side.
steps.terutzMaskana: We learn from the animal comparison, which is מופנה on both sides. The תורה made it that way on purpose.

steps.title: A lenient version of the rule about free words
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא gives a more lenient version of רבי אלעזר's rule: even a גזירה שוה with no free words can be used, but it can be refuted. A one-sided one depends on a disagreement, and a two-sided one cannot be refuted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא teaches it in the name of רבי אלעזר in a lenient way. If a גזירה שוה is not free at all, we learn from it, but we can refute it. If it is free on one side: according to רבי ישמעאל we learn from it and cannot refute it; according to רבנן we learn from it and can refute it. If it is free on both sides, everyone agrees we learn from it and cannot refute it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, more lenient version of רבי אלעזר's rule about how far we can rely on a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sets up three levels: not free at all, free on one side, and free on both sides. 'Refuting' means pointing out a logical difference between the two cases that cancels the comparison. This version is lenient because it allows learning even from a comparison with no free words at all, as long as no one can refute it.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two topics based on the same word appearing in both
We learn: the comparison can teach a law
We refute: a logical difference between the cases can cancel the comparison
In the lenient direction: here, more willing to accept the comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: not free at all means we learn but can refute. Free on one side depends on רבי ישמעאל versus רבנן. Free on both sides means everyone agrees we learn and cannot refute.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'lenient' does not mean a lenient halacha. It means this version is more willing to accept a גזירה שוה as a valid source.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, teaches it
in the name of Rabbi Elazar in a lenient way:
Any verbal analogy
that is not free at all
we learn from it, but we can refute it;
if it is free on one side,
according to Rabbi Yishmael we learn from it and cannot refute it;
according to the Rabbis we learn from it, but we can refute it;
if it is free on both sides,
everyone agrees we learn from it and cannot refute it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, more lenient version of the rule about free words that the sugya has been relying on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not free at all: we learn but can refute. Free on one side: רבי ישמעאל says we cannot refute, רבנן say we can. Free on both sides: everyone agrees we cannot refute.

steps.title: What is the difference for the Rabbis?
steps.stepSummary: Under this version, רבנן give the same result for a one-sided comparison and a comparison with no free words: learn, but refutable. So the גמרא asks what difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the Rabbis, what difference is there between a comparison free on one side and one that is not free at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that, according to רבנן, two of the levels seem to have the same rule. It asks what the difference between them could be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, a comparison free on one side and one not free at all both get 'we learn, but we can refute.' If they act the same, why does it matter whether a comparison has one free side? The גמרא is looking for a practical difference.

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis,
what difference is there between
an analogy free on one side
and one that is not free at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין מוּפְנָה מִצַּד אֶחָד לְשֶׁאֵינָהּ מוּפְנָה כׇּל עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the lenient version from step 2, because two of its levels seem to have the same rule for רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical difference, according to רבנן, between a גזירה שוה free on one side and one not free at all.

steps.title: The difference shows up when two comparisons clash
steps.stepSummary: When a one-sided comparison and a comparison with no free words point in opposite directions, and neither can be refuted, we drop the one with no free words and follow the one-sided one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is in a case where you find one comparison free on one side and one not free at all, and neither one can be refuted. Then we drop the one that is not free at all and learn from the one free on one side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference matters only when two comparisons conflict. Then the one with at least one free side wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, each kind of comparison works the same way for רבנן. When they compete, though, being free on one side makes a comparison stronger, so it beats the one with no free words. This matches step 1, where the comparison free on both sides beat the one-sided one.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of it
A logical refutation that cancels a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: When comparisons clash, the one with more free words wins: free on both sides beats free on one side, and free on one side beats not free at all.

phrases.english: The difference is where you find
phrases.notes: He means two comparisons that lead to opposite rulings, so we cannot follow both.

phrases.english: one that is free on one side
and one that is not free at all,
and neither does this one have a refutation,
nor does that one have a refutation;
we leave aside the one that is not free at all,
and we derive from the one that is free on one side.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ הֵיכָא דְּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ מוּפְנָה מִצַּד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by giving a case where the two levels lead to different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When two comparisons that cannot be refuted contradict each other, we follow the one free on one side over the one not free at all.

steps.title: What refutation knocks down the man and sea monster comparison?
steps.stepSummary: Under רב אחא בריה דרבא's version, a one-sided גזירה שוה can be used unless it is refuted. So the גמרא asks what the refutation is in the case of אדם and תנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, what refutation is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. Under the lenient version, a one-sided comparison only falls if someone can refute it, so what refutes the comparison between man and sea monster? This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the comparison between אדם and תנין was rejected because it was only free on one side. But רב אחא בריה דרבא says a one-sided comparison works unless there is a logical refutation. So the גמרא must now find that refutation, or else the rejection does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a logical difference that breaks a comparison

phrases.english: And here, what refutation is there?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the comparison between a person and the sea monster that the גמרא turned down earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the new lenient version (refutable, but usable) back to the earlier rejection of the man and sea monster comparison
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What logical refutation breaks the one-sided גזירה שוה between אדם and תנין

steps.title: A person can become impure while alive
steps.stepSummary: The refutation: a person is special because he can become טמא while alive, unlike an animal or a sea monster.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one can refute it: what is special about a person? He becomes impure while alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the refutation. A person is different because he can become impure even while he is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal only becomes impure after it dies, and a sea monster does not become impure at all. Because a person has this special stringency, you cannot use him to teach about a sea monster. So the one-sided comparison is refuted and falls.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about a person? (the standard way to open a refutation)

phrases.english: Because one can refute it:
What is special about a person? He becomes impure while alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by naming the refutation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אדם has a unique stringency (he becomes impure while alive), so he cannot be compared to a תנין

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: animals are 'formed' like a person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר's reason is that the תורה uses the word יצירה (forming) for animals just as it does for אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is רבי מאיר's reason, because 'forming' is said about it, just like a person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source for רבי מאיר's ruling that an animal-shaped miscarriage makes the mother impure. The word 'forming' is used for both animals and people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the approach the גמרא already used: the comparison is built on the shared word יצירה. Because the same word appears by animals and by אדם, an animal-shaped miscarriage is treated like a human birth for the laws of טומאת לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forming: the word the תורה uses for how God made people and animals

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: And likewise, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Meir:
since 'forming' is said about it, just like a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier derivation with an amora's statement of רבי מאיר's reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר learns animal-shaped miscarriages from אדם through the shared word יצירה

steps.title: Then a mountain-shaped miscarriage should count too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי objects: the word 'forms' is also used for mountains, so a mountain-shaped miscarriage should make the mother impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: if so, a woman who miscarries something shaped like a mountain should be impure from childbirth, as it says 'For He forms the mountains and creates the wind.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי attacks the rule. If the word 'forming' is enough, then mountains should count too, because a פסוק says God 'forms mountains.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge stretches the logic to a silly result. If every use of the word יצירה links to אדם, then a mountain-shaped miscarriage would bring טומאת לידה, which nobody holds.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so: introduces an absurd result of what was just said
Impure with the impurity of a woman who gave birth

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
If that is so, a woman who miscarries the shape of a mountain:
its mother should be impure from childbirth,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי הִנֵּה יוֹצֵר הָרִים וּבוֹרֵא רוּחַ״?
phrases.english: as it says, 'For behold, He forms the mountains and creates the wind'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's יצירה source by extending it to mountains
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from the word יצירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word יצירה also appears by mountains, so the same logic would make a mountain-shaped miscarriage טמאה לידה, which is absurd

steps.title: A woman can't deliver a mountain, only a 'clod'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers: a woman cannot miscarry a mountain. At most it is shaped like a stone, and that is called a גוש (clod), not a mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: does she miscarry a mountain? It is a stone she miscarries, and that is called a 'clod.'
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. Something small enough to be miscarried is not a 'mountain' at all; it is a clod, and the פסוק does not say 'forming' about clods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer limits the comparison to the actual thing named in the פסוק. A small stone-like shape has its own name, גוש, so the word 'forms mountains' does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A clod or lump of earth/stone

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַר מִי קָא מַפְּלָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Does she miscarry a mountain?
It is a stone that she miscarries,
and that is called a 'clod.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's mountain challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: what is miscarried is not a 'mountain'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mountain-shaped miscarriage falls under 'He forms mountains'
steps.terutzMaskana: A miscarried stone shape is a גוש, which the פסוק does not mention

steps.title: Then a shapeless 'רוח' miscarriage should count
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי pushes again: the same פסוק says 'creates רוח,' and בריאה (creating) is said about אדם, so a shapeless miscarriage should bring טומאת לידה. The extra word 'creates' shows the word is free for a comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a woman who miscarries a 'רוח' should be impure from childbirth, since 'creating' is said about it just like a person, as it says 'and creates רוח.' And if you say the word is not free: since the פסוק could have written 'forms mountains and רוח' but wrote 'and creates רוח,' learn from this that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי brings a second, stronger challenge. A shapeless miscarriage should count, because the פסוק uses the word 'creates' for רוח, just as the תורה uses it for people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He also blocks the easy answer that the word is needed for its plain meaning. The פסוק could have just said 'forms mountains and רוח.' Adding the word 'creates' shows it is extra, so it is free to be used for a גזירה שוה. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Creating: the word used for how God made people
To make a word free (extra) so it can be used for a גזירה שוה

steps.confusionAlert: רוח here is not a 'spirit' or a breath of wind coming out. It means a miscarriage with no real shape, and the challenge plays on the word רוח in the פסוק.

phrases.english: If that is so, a woman who miscarries a 'ruaḥ':
phrases.notes: רוח means wind, but here it means a shapeless thing. The challenge uses both meanings of the same word.

phrases.english: its mother should be impure from childbirth,
since 'creating' is said about it, just like a person,
as it is written, 'and creates the wind'?
And if you say it is not free,
since it could have written 'who forms the mountains and the wind,'
and instead it is written 'and creates the wind,'
learn from it that it is there to make it free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the mountain challenge is answered, רבי אמי brings a second challenge from the other half of the same פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of learning טומאת לידה from shared creation words with אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Creates רוח' uses the same word בריאה as אדם, and the extra word shows it is free, so a shapeless miscarriage should be טמאה לידה, which is absurd

steps.title: A verse from נביאים cannot teach a law of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers רבי אמי's push. We learn laws of the תורה from verses in the תורה, not from verses in נביאים or כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learn matters of the תורה from matters of the תורה. We do not learn matters of the תורה from דברי קבלה, the words of tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers רבי אמי's challenge about the word 'creates' (בריאה). That word comes from a verse in נביאים, and you cannot build a law of the תורה on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי wanted to compare the word 'creates' in the verse about mountains and wind to 'creates' said about אדם, and so make a shapeless miscarriage bring טומאת לידה. רבי חייא בר אבא says the comparison is invalid. A law of טומאה comes from the תורה, so it can only be learned from a verse in the תורה itself. This answers the challenge from Step 10. רבי יוחנן's יצירה source from Step 7 still stands, because the word יצירה for animals and for אדם is written in the תורה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: we derive / we learn (a law from a verse)
matters written in the חמישה חומשי תורה
words of tradition: verses from נביאים or כתובים

steps.whatToRemember: A law of the תורה cannot be derived from a verse in נביאים or כתובים. That is why the comparison from the verse in עמוס fails.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used all over ש״ס. Verses from נביאים and כתובים can teach or support ideas, but they cannot be the source of a law of the תורה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי חייא בר אבא is answering רבי אמי.

phrases.english: We learn matters of the Torah from matters of the Torah,
but we do not learn matters of the Torah
from the words of tradition.
phrases.notes: The verse 'forms mountains and creates wind' is from עמוס 4:13, a book of נביאים, not the תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דָּנִין דִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's second challenge from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the source of the comparison: a verse from נביאים cannot create a Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'creates' in עמוס is free, so it can be compared to 'creates' said about אדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: A comparison from נביאים cannot teach a Torah law, so the challenge falls away.

steps.title: A new reason for רבי מאיר: the eyes look human
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. רבי מאיר's reason is that these animals have eyes similar to a person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is רבי מאיר's reason. It is because their eyes are similar to those of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different explanation of רבי מאיר's view. Here the reason is the shape of the eyes, not a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבי יוחנן's reason was based on the word יצירה. Now a different report of רבי יוחנן gives a reason based on how the fetus looks. Because the eyes of these animals resemble human eyes, the fetus is treated like a human birth, and the mother is טמאה לידה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new and separate reason, not a continuation of the יצירה approach. It comes from a different student quoting רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Meir:
since their eyes are similar to those of a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אמי's challenges to the יצירה reason are answered, a different report of רבי יוחנן gives another reason for רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, an animal-shaped miscarriage makes the mother טמאה לידה because its eyes resemble human eyes.

steps.title: Then a snake-shaped miscarriage should also count
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is human-like eyes, a snake's round eye should also make the mother טמאה לידה. And if so, why doesn't the משנה mention a snake?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a woman who miscarries something shaped like a snake should be impure as after a birth, since a snake's eyeball is round like a person's! And if you say that is indeed the law, then the משנה should teach the case of a snake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the eyes reason. It would include a snake too, yet the משנה lists animals and birds but not a snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake's eyeball is round like a human's, so the eyes reason seems to cover it. You could simply accept that and say a snake does count. But then the problem is that the משנה should have listed a snake as its case. The challenge is really about the משנה's choice of examples.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introduces a challenge from the logic just stated)
impure with the impurity of a woman after giving birth
indeed so; that is the law
let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: But if so,
a woman who miscarries something in the form of a snake,
its mother should be impure with the impurity of birth,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹלה כְּשֶׁל אָדָם!
phrases.english: since its eyeball is round like a person's!
And if you say, indeed it is so,
then let it teach a snake!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the eyes reason given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's eyes reason for רבי מאיר, together with the משנה's list of cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eyes reason should include a snake. If a snake is included, the משנה should have taught that case.

steps.title: Why the משנה chose animals and not a snake
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught a snake, we would think the רבנן argue only there. Teaching animals shows that they argue even where the תורה says יצירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught a snake, I would have said the רבנן argue with רבי מאיר only about a snake, because 'forming' is not written about it. But about domestic and wild animals they would not argue, because 'forming' is written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a snake really is included by רבי מאיר. The משנה chose animals on purpose to show how far the רבנן's disagreement goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About animals the תורה does use the word יצירה, which might seem to make them closer to a person. If the משנה had listed only a snake, we might think the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר about animals. By listing animals, the משנה teaches that the רבנן argue even in that stronger case, and the snake is then understood on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: By the eyes reason, רבי מאיר includes a snake too. The משנה lists animals to show that the רבנן argue even there, where the תורה writes יצירה.

phrases.english: If it had taught a snake,
I would have said:
it is about a snake that the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Meir,
since 'forming' is not written about it,
but about a domestic or wild animal, they do not disagree,
since 'forming' is written about them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, meaning 'about them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13 about why the משנה does not mention a snake.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's choice of example (a 'not only this, but even that' style answer).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If only a snake were taught, we would think the רבנן agree about animals because the Torah writes יצירה about them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches animals to show the רבנן argue even there. A snake is included by רבי מאיר's reason.

steps.title: A blemish law suggests animal eyes are not like human eyes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's claim that animals have eyes like a person's. A משנה about מומין treats a human-like round eye as a defect in an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding blemishes, a משנה teaches that an animal whose eyeball is round like a person's counts as blemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from Step 12. If animal eyes were already like human eyes, a human-like eye would not be a defect in an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts as a מום only when it is unusual for that animal. Since a 'round eye like a person's' is listed as a מום, normal animal eyes must be different from human eyes. That seems to knock out רבי יוחנן's reason for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes or defects in an animal
The eyeball, or the round part of the eye

phrases.english: But regarding blemishes, it teaches it:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בכורות about which defects let a firstborn animal be slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁגַּלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם!
phrases.english: one whose eyeball is round like a person's!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's reason from Step 12 and challenges it from another משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that these animals' eyes resemble a person's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about מומין treats a human-like round eye as abnormal in an animal, so animal eyes are normally not human-like.

steps.title: One source refers to the pupil, the other to the eyeball in its socket
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: animals' pupils resemble a person's, but the whole eyeball sitting in its socket does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the black part of the eye, and that one is about the eyeball in its socket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the two sources talk about different parts of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's 'similar eyes' is about the אוכמא, the dark pupil, which is like a person's. The משנה about מומין is about the ציריא, the eyeball in its socket, and that is normally different in an animal. So both statements are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources don't really clash
The black part of the eye, the pupil
The eyeball as it sits in its socket

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the black part of the eye,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's statement: the pupil is like a person's.

phrases.english: that one is about the eyeball in its socket.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — הָא בְּאוּכָּמָא, הָא בְּצִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different part of the eye
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to talk about the same eye feature, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pupil is like a person's; the eyeball in its socket is not. רבי יוחנן's reason stands.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: the animals' eyes face forward like a person's
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי gives a different reason for רבי מאיר: these animals have eyes on the front of the head, like a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: This is רבי מאיר's reason, because their eyes face forward like a person's.
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of רבי מאיר's opinion begins. The point is no longer how the eye looks, but where it sits on the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ינאי, the human-like feature is that the eyes face forward. This new reason now has to fit every case where רבי מאיר says the mother is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'go in front of them', meaning the eyes face forward

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Meir:
since their eyes go in front of them
like those of a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reason for רבי מאיר, alongside רבי יוחנן's from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר makes the mother טמאה because the creature's eyes face forward like a person's.

steps.title: Birds' eyes don't face forward, yet רבי מאיר says טמאה
steps.stepSummary: Challenge to רבי ינאי: birds' eyes are not in front, but רבי מאיר still makes the mother טמאה for a bird shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a bird, whose eyes do not face forward, and רבי מאיר says she is טמאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי's reason with the case of a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If forward-facing eyes are the key, a bird with side eyes should not count. But רבי מאיר counts a bird too, so רבי ינאי's reason seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure; here, the mother has טומאת לידה

phrases.english: But there is a bird,
whose eyes do not face forward,
and Rabbi Meir says that she is impure!
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי מאיר makes a woman טמאה if she miscarries something shaped like a bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי עוֹף, דְּאֵין עֵינָיו הוֹלְכוֹת לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's reason from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's reason that forward-facing eyes are the key
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds lack forward-facing eyes, yet רבי מאיר still makes the mother טמאה for a bird shape.

steps.title: אביי: רבי מאיר means only owls
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי מאיר's bird case is only owls, whose eyes face forward. For other birds, רבי מאיר agrees she is not טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי מאיר is talking about the little owl and the great owl, but not other birds.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי saves רבי ינאי's reason by narrowing which birds רבי מאיר meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Owls have forward-facing eyes, so they fit רבי ינאי's reason. The word 'bird' in the משנה is read as meaning only these birds. Other birds do not make the mother טמאה even for רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is about the little owl and the great owl,
but with other birds, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: 'bird' means only owls
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seemed to include every bird, even ones with side eyes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר includes only owls, which have forward-facing eyes, so רבי ינאי's reason holds.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר is right for animals, the חכמים for birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge אביי. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס sides with רבי מאיר for animals but with the חכמים for birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: רבי מאיר's view seems right for domestic and wild animals, and the חכמים' view seems right for birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge אביי's answer. This step only sets up the source; the actual attack is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס splits between animals and birds. The next step will ask how this fits אביי, who says רבי מאיר's birds are owls with forward-facing eyes, just like the animals.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
The words of Rabbi Meir seem correct
for a domestic animal and a wild animal,
and the words of the Sages for birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא as the source for a challenge to אביי's answer in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that רבי מאיר's birds are owls with forward-facing eyes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא treats birds differently from animals; the next step shows why that clashes with אביי.

steps.title: If the birds are owls, why treat them differently from animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which birds the ברייתא means. If it means owls, they have forward-facing eyes like animals, so why would רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס split them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Which birds? If you say the little owl and the great owl, what is different about domestic and wild animals, whose eyes face forward like a person's? Owls have that too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא. If רבי מאיר's birds are only owls, as אביי said, the ברייתא's split makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי ינאי's reason, animals count because their eyes face forward. Owls' eyes also face forward, so they should be treated just like animals. Yet רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס agrees with רבי מאיר for animals and not for birds, which puts אביי's answer in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a possible answer that the גמרא then knocks down

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not attacking רבי מאיר himself. It challenges אביי's claim that רבי מאיר's 'birds' mean only owls.

phrases.english: What birds?
If you say the little owl and the great owl,
what is different about a domestic and wild animal
that their eyes face forward like a person's?
The little owl and the great owl too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the attack from the ברייתא quoted in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that רבי מאיר's birds are owls with forward-facing eyes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owls share the forward-facing eyes that make animals count, so a ruler who agrees with רבי מאיר for animals should agree for owls too. Since the ברייתא splits animals from birds, the birds can't be owls.

steps.title: So the ברייתא must mean other birds, and then רבי מאיר argues about them too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot mean owls, so it must mean other birds. That would show רבי מאיר disagrees with the חכמים even about other birds, which goes against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means other birds. So we learn that רבי מאיר disagrees about other birds too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 21. The ברייתא's split must be about ordinary birds, so it seems רבי מאיר argued about ordinary birds too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס said he sides with the חכמים about birds. That only makes sense if רבי מאיר disagreed about those same birds. But אביי said רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים about ordinary birds, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Other birds (birds that are not owls)
From this we can learn / it follows that

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it means other birds.
From this we learn that רבי מאיר
disagrees about other birds as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in steps 20-21 by drawing the conclusion that goes against אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר only argued about owls (step 19).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Siding with the חכמים about ordinary birds implies there was a real argument about ordinary birds, so רבי מאיר must have held they count as a child.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: רבי מאיר only argued about owls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is missing words. Read correctly, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס agrees with the חכמים about other birds because רבי מאיר himself agrees with them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing, and this is what it teaches: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says, רבי מאיר seems right about domestic and wild animals, and the same for the little owl and the great owl. The חכמים seem right about other birds, because even רבי מאיר only argued with them about the little owl and great owl. About other birds, he agrees with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by saying the ברייתא is incomplete. With the missing words added, the ברייתא actually supports אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the חכמים seem right about other birds' do not mean there was a dispute there. They mean everyone, even רבי מאיר, agrees about other birds. The only real argument is about animals and owls, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words (fill in the gap)
A domestic animal and a wild animal
Two kinds of owl (little owl and great owl)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'the חכמים seem right about other birds' as taking a side in an argument. After the fix, it means רבי מאיר agrees with them there, so there is no argument at all.

phrases.english: Words are missing from the ברייתא,
and this is what it teaches:
רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says:
The words of רבי מאיר seem right
about a domestic animal and a wild animal,
and the same is true for the little owl and the great owl,
and the words of the חכמים seem right about other birds,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף רַבִּי מֵאִיר לֹא נֶחְלַק עִמָּהֶם
phrases.english: because even רבי מאיר did not disagree with them
except about the little owl and the great owl,
but about other birds, he agrees with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by fixing the reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that רבי מאיר argued about all birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read fully, the ברייתא says רבי מאיר only argued about owls and agrees about other birds, just like אביי.

steps.title: A ברייתא says bird shapes must be checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: animal shapes are a child for רבי מאיר and not for the חכמים, but bird shapes must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said, a woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic or wild animal: according to רבי מאיר, it is a child; according to the חכמים, it is not a child. For birds, it must be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי. Step 25 will explain how it proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats animals and birds differently. For animals the answer is simple, but for birds it says the shape must be checked. That hints that not all birds have the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: A child (it counts as a real birth, making the mother טמאה)

phrases.english: And indeed it was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said:
A woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic or wild animal:
according to רבי מאיר, it is a child,
and according to the חכמים, it is not a child.
With birds, it must be checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending אביי, the גמרא now brings a separate source to support him.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר makes a difference between owls and other birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק saying bird shapes must be checked.

steps.title: Checking only makes sense for רבי מאיר, who splits owls from other birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. The checking must follow רבי מאיר, who says owls count and other birds do not, so we must check which kind of bird it looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom must it be checked? Is it not according to רבי מאיר, who said: a little owl or great owl, yes; other birds, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the ברייתא proves אביי. The only reason to check a bird shape is to tell an owl apart from other birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, no bird shape counts, so there is nothing to check. Checking only matters if some birds count and some do not. That is exactly רבי מאיר's view as אביי explained it: owls yes, other birds no.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not...? (shows the answer is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי מאיר only treats owl shapes as a real child, because their eyes face forward. For other birds he agrees with the חכמים. The proof from 'birds must be checked' is rejected in the next step.

phrases.english: According to whom must it be checked?
Is it not according to רבי מאיר, who said:
a little owl or a great owl, yes, it counts,
other birds, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא in step 24 proves אביי's view.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split within רבי מאיר between owls and other birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling 'with birds, it must be checked,' which only makes sense if some birds count and others do not.

steps.title: The checking could follow the חכמים instead
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the ברייתא proves nothing about רבי מאיר. The checking of bird shapes could follow the חכמים, who count owls but not other birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב איקא, said: No. 'It must be checked' follows the חכמים, who say owls count and other birds do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 25. It offers another way to read the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the checking must follow רבי מאיר. רב אחא says it could just as well follow the חכמים, who also draw a line between owls and other birds. So the ברייתא no longer proves that רבי מאיר splits owls from other birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of owls (a little owl and a great owl)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said:
No, 'it must be checked' follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: He means the line 'bird shapes must be checked' in the ברייתא from step 24.

phrases.english: who say: owl shapes, yes, she is impure,
other birds, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the ברייתא shows רבי מאיר's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The checking can be explained just as well by the חכמים, who also split owls from other birds.

steps.title: Why would the חכמים count owls but not animals?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say animal shapes do not count. So why would owl shapes count for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about owls compared to domestic and wild animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading of the חכמים' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say a discharge that looks like an animal does not make the woman impure. If even animals do not count, it seems odd that a bird like an owl would count. The new reading in step 26 needs a reason for this difference.

phrases.english: And what is different about owls
from domestic and wild animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קַרְיָא וְקִיפוֹפָא מִבְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חכמים count owl shapes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If animals do not count for the חכמים, owls should not count either.

steps.title: Owls have cheeks like a person
steps.stepSummary: Owls count for the חכמים because they have cheeks like a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they have cheeks like a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals have eyes in the front, but for the חכמים that is not enough. Owls also have human-like cheeks, and that is what makes their shape close enough to a person to count.
steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, owls are special because of their human-like cheeks. So the ברייתא of 'checking' can follow the חכמים, and it proves nothing about רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Since they have cheeks like a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a physical feature that sets owls apart
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Owls should be no better than animals for the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owls have human-like cheeks, so they count even for the חכמים.

steps.title: Can a father marry off an animal-shaped baby girl?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: according to רבי מאיר, who treats an animal-shaped birth as a real child, does a father's acceptance of קידושין for such a girl work? It would matter for whether the husband may marry her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: According to רבי מאיר, who says an animal in a woman's womb is a full child, what if her father accepted קידושין for her? What difference would it make? Whether the husband is forbidden to marry her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רבי ירמיה asks a question that takes רבי מאיר's view to its extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר says the animal-shaped birth is a real child, maybe it can also be married off. A father may accept קידושין for his young daughter. If this marriage works, the husband would be forbidden to marry her sister, because a man may not marry his wife's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
What practical difference does it make?
To be forbidden to her sister

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
According to Rabbi Meir, who said

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא,
phrases.english: an animal in a woman's womb is a full child,
if her father accepted betrothal for her, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Picture a female animal-shaped birth that is treated as a daughter. A father can accept betrothal for his young daughter.

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
For the husband to be forbidden to marry her sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that builds on רבי מאיר's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קידושין works for an animal-shaped ולד according to רבי מאיר

steps.title: Such a creature cannot even live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this creature can live at all. רב יהודה said in the name of רב that רבי מאיר counted it only because animals of its kind can live, not because this one can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this saying it lives? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי מאיר said it only because creatures of its kind survive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's sister is forbidden only while the wife is alive. רב יהודה said in the name of רב that this creature does not live. רבי מאיר counted it only because animals of its type survive. So the question about marrying her sister has no real case.

phrases.english: Is this to say that it lives?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
Rabbi Meir said it
only because creatures of its kind survive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of the question in step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question assumes the creature lives, but רבי מאיר himself holds that it does not.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה was trying to make רבי זירא laugh
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the question was not serious. רבי ירמיה was trying to make רבי זירא laugh, but רבי זירא did not laugh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Up to here רבי ירמיה tried to bring רבי זירא to laughter, but he did not laugh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this short section by explaining that the question was only a joke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was not serious, so there is nothing to answer. The case is impossible, since the creature cannot live. רבי ירמיה was trying to get רבי זירא to laugh, and רבי זירא stayed serious.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about קידושין for an animal-shaped ולד was only a joke. Such a creature does not live, even according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ya'akov said:
Up to here Rabbi Yirmeya tried to bring
Rabbi Zeira to laughter,
but he did not laugh.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן הֱבִיאוֹ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא לִידֵי גִּיחוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why step 29's question was asked even though step 30 showed it has no real case
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question was not serious. It was an attempt to make רבי זירא laugh.

steps.title: The statement itself: רבי מאיר's reason is that its kind can live
steps.stepSummary: Using the word גופא, the גמרא returns to רב יהודה's quote of רב. רבי מאיר counted an animal-shaped birth only because creatures of its kind are able to live. Then רב ירמיה מדפתי is introduced to comment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי מאיר said this only because creatures of its kind can live. רב ירמיה מדפתי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement it quoted a moment ago, so it can study that statement properly. The step ends by introducing רב ירמיה מדפתי, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30 this statement was used as a quick tool to answer רבי ירמיה's joke question. Now the גמרא repeats it to examine it directly. The key point is that רבי מאיר is not looking at whether this particular creature can live. He is looking at whether its kind can live.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself." The גמרא is going back to study a statement it quoted earlier.
In its kind, meaning other creatures of the same type

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a needless repeat of step 30. There the statement was borrowed to answer a question. Here the גמרא brings it back on purpose to examine it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines exactly why רבי מאיר holds his view: it depends on the kind of creature, not on this specific one. The upcoming comment builds on that.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Rabbi Meir did not say it
phrases.notes: "It" means his ruling that a woman who gives birth to an animal-shaped creature is impure as after a birth.

phrases.english: except because creatures of its kind can live.
Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the joke exchange in step 31, the גמרא returns to the statement of רב יהודה in the name of רב that was quoted in step 30, so it can examine it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped birth as a real birth only because creatures of its kind are able to live.
